_about: Therapy classes a clinician may consider for each Insight Rx finding. Summaries of published guidelines, for clinician review; never a prescription. Ordered within each finding by guideline strength. Sponsorship never enters this file.

classes.label: Anti-VEGF intravitreal therapy
classes.summary: First-line for centre-involved diabetic macular edema with vision loss and an option for proliferative DR. Given by a retina specialist, so the referral is the action.
classes.source: AAO Diabetic Retinopathy Preferred Practice Pattern; DRCR Retina Network Protocols T and S

classes.label: Tighten glucose, blood pressure and lipids
classes.summary: Optimising glycaemia, blood pressure and lipids reduces the risk or slows progression of retinopathy. Intensify gradually: rapid HbA1c falls can transiently worsen DR.
classes.source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes, Section 12 (Retinopathy)

classes.label: Fenofibrate (adjunct)
classes.summary: Slowed DR progression in FIELD and ACCORD-Eye and reduced progression to referable DR in LENS. Consider in non-proliferative DR, especially with dyslipidaemia.

classes.label: ACE inhibitor or ARB
classes.summary: Recommended for hypertension in diabetes, and first choice when albuminuria is present. Use one, never both.
classes.source: ADA Standards of Care, Sections 10 and 11; KDIGO 2022 Diabetes in CKD

classes.label: SGLT2 inhibitor
classes.summary: Kidney and heart protection in type 2 diabetes with CKD (eGFR 20 or above), independent of glucose lowering.
classes.source: KDIGO 2022 Diabetes in CKD; ADA Standards of Care, Section 11

classes.label: Non-steroidal MRA (finerenone)
classes.summary: Add for type 2 diabetes with persistent albuminuria despite a maximally tolerated ACE inhibitor or ARB, with normal potassium.
classes.source: KDIGO 2022 Diabetes in CKD; FIDELIO-DKD and FIGARO-DKD

classes.label: GLP-1 receptor agonist
classes.summary: Glucose and weight lowering with proven cardiovascular benefit, and kidney benefit (FLOW). Check retinopathy status first: semaglutide carries a label warning on DR complications.
classes.source: ADA Standards of Care, Sections 9 and 10; SUSTAIN-6; FLOW (NEJM 2024)

classes.label: Painful neuropathy agents
classes.summary: First-line options for painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy, alongside glucose control and annual foot examination.
classes.source: ADA Standards of Care, Section 12 (Neuropathy); AAN 2021 guideline

classes.label: Aldose reductase inhibitor
classes.summary: Approved for diabetic neuropathy in Japan, China and India; not FDA approved. A target story rather than a US option today.
